Q: using AZCOPY with only connectionstring A:

Under Linux I managed to solve this with just the az command, so not the extra azcopy command. I hope this is not off topic.

export AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING="SECRET"

az storage azcopy blob upload --container container1 --source /tmp/afile.img --connection-string $AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING
  • Tested with az 2.82.0 on Debian 12. In bash shell (which is the default)
  • Installed from Microsoft apt package source as described here: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-linux?view=azure-cli-latest&pivots=apt
  • I later realized that I can even omit the --connection-string ... in the command. Not sure yet whether this is always true.
  • Did NOT work with az version 2.74.0 on Debian 13 from default Debian package sources

Q: EXIF UserComment inside nested IFD Entry is truncated when writing entries to ByteArrayOutputStream A:

As mentioned in Twelvemonkeys/1240 the incorrect value you see is a bug in the Twelvemonkeys library regarding writing nested IFDs and incorrect calculation of the space needed causing possible overwrite of previous values.

However, it is probably incorrect to write the EXIF.TAG_DATE_TIME_ORIGINAL in the top-level IFD. You should only write the TIFF.TAG_DATE_TIME here, and move the other to the Exif sub-IFD. Moving the tag to the Exif-IFD also happens to work around the issue, as the bug only surface if there are tags in the top-level IFD after the sub-IFD. 😀

Q: rearrange some columns in R alphabetically A:

Here is another answer using an auxiliary function.

suppressPackageStartupMessages(
  library(dplyr)
)
set.seed(123)  ## for sake of reproducibility
n <- 6
test_df <- data.frame(id=1:n, 
                      date=seq.Date(as.Date("2020-12-26"), as.Date("2020-12-31"), "day"),
                      group=rep(LETTERS[1:2], n/2),
                      age=sample(18:30, n, replace=TRUE),
                      type=factor(paste("type", 1:n)),
                      ampicillin2 = rnorm(n),
                      amoxicillin = rnorm(n),
                      penicillin = rnorm(n),
                      ciprofloxacin = rnorm(n),
                      gentamicin = rnorm(n),
                      ceftriaxone = rnorm(n),
                      tobramycin = rnorm(n),
                      org = rep(LETTERS[1:2], n/2),
                      sample = rep(LETTERS[1:2], n/2)
)

sort_cols <- function(X, cols) {
  cols <- select(X, {{cols}}) %>% names()
  i_old <- which(names(X) %in% cols)
  i_new <- order(cols) + min(i_old) - 1L
  X[i_old] <- X[i_new]
  names(X)[i_old] <- names(X)[i_new]
  X
}

test_df %>%
  sort_cols(ampicillin2:tobramycin)
